findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
There were two employees working at the time of the inspection, one employee was a certified food protection manager and the other employee did not have any food certificates. Discussed the need of at least a food handler certificate if handling food, drinks, or clean dishes. Be sure that all employees obtain a food handler certificate within 30 days of hire if not already a certified food protection manager. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the coffee dispenser (labeled flavored) to have an accumulation of debris on the outer part of the dispenser. Discussed with PIC and dispenser was cleaned. Ensure that coffee dispensers are cleaned as frequent of necessary to prevent accumulation. 

- The counter underneath the espresso machine was also observed to have an accumulation of coffee grounds. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that countertop is cleaned at the end of the night or as often as necessary to prevent accumulation. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following locations were observed with an accumulation of soil debris/residues that will need to be cleaned and sanitized:
-The bottom of the double door cooler int he store room
-The underneath portion of the coffee dispensers along the wall, especially the “flavored” coffee dispenser
Ensure these locations and all NonFOOD-contact are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
5-402.15: The mop bucket was observed to not have been dumped since last night’s cleaning crew. After discussion with the PIC, it was determined the mop water was stored like this to prevent fly eggs in the mop head. In order to correct the disposal of the mop water and to properly allow the mop to air dry while preventing pests, an action plan has been established that the mop water will be dumped after each use and the mop head will be allowed to air dry. While the mop head is air drying, a fan will be placed in this location creating a breeze to assist the mop in air drying and to help create an air curtain to prevent fruit flies from inhabiting the mop head. 
5-402.15: A tank for liquid waste retention shall be thoroughly flushed and drained in a sanitary manner during the servicing operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The floor in the store room is observed to have a build-up of residues/soil. Discussion with PIC took place to have the floors in the store room cleaned more thoroughly at the end of each shift. Ensure that under and next to equipment are also cleaned during this process. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The gasket of the single door cooler is observed to be in a state of disrepair. Ensure that this gasket is properly repairs to allow the door to completely seal and to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the ice machine to be soiled with mold and pinkish mildew. The ice machine and other equipment food-contact surfaces must be clean to sight and touch. Ensure the ice machine is cleaned at a frequency so it is maintained clean. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the syrup shelf/rack to have an accumulation of syrup and other debris. Ensure this is cleaned frequently so it is maintained clean. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: Observed the mop stored inside the mop bucket. The mop bucket also had wastewater inside it. Ensure the mop is placed in a position that allows it to air dry and wastewater is discarded after use. 
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC with food manager certification was not present upon arrival of inspectors. Employee that was the PIC upon arrival of inspectors stated manager was at the 7th Street location. Manager returned later during the inspection. Manager stated he is between the two locations at the hospital multiple times a day in addition to covering at other locations as needed (breaks, etc.). The need for a certified food manager at all times at each location was discussed.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee did not wash hands prior to putting on a glove to handle baked goods. Proper handwashing prior to glove use was discussed. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed prior to putting on gloves to handle food and after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11 Evidence was observed that indicated the handsink has been used as a dump sink. Discoloration, splash, and a small amount of grounds were observed in the handsink basin. Proper use of the handsink was discussed.  
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using the handsink for any other purposes.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.13 Paper towel and hand soap dispensers were observed on the walls by the prep sink and 3 part sink. The soap dispenser at the prep sink had soap in it, while all other dispensers were empty. Manager will place a work order to remove the dispensers from the aforementioned areas. 
A sink used for food preparation or utensil washing, or a service sink or curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water or similar wastes, may not be provided with the handwashing aids and devices required for a handwashing sink as specified under §§ 6-301.11 and 6-301.12 and ¶ 5-501.16(C).
All sinks not used for handwashing should not be supplied with handwashing aids/devices.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 A half dozen fruit flies were observed on the wall adjacent to the soda machine up front. A dozen fruit flies were observed on the mop stored damp in the mopsink basin. Fly management was discussed, including use of fly strips in appropriate locations and general cleaning.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Lid to ice machine was open upon arrival of inspectors. Employee was up front making drinks and not retrieving ice at the time. Inspector closed the lid. Ensure the lid to the ice machine is closed between uses, especially with the presence of fruit flies in the back room.
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp, soiled wiping cloth was observed in the middle compartment of the 3 part sink. Employee stated it was used earlier and came from the sani-bucket. Proper storage of wiping cloths between uses was discussed. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Scoop in drink powder was stored with the handle submerged in the product. Scoop was repositioned to allow for proper storage of the handle up out of product.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12 Floors throughout had varying amounts of sticky buildup, especially in the back room. Debris accumulation was observed under the ice machine, soda syrup storage rack, and the 2 door upright cooler. 
Mold accumulation was also observed on the domed cover inside the floor drain under the 3 part sink. 
Clean the floors and the drain in the aforementioned areas
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

6-501.16 Damp mop was stored in the basin of the mopsink. Ensure proper storage of mop between uses to eliminate a potential harborage location for fruit flies.
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.114 Unused Gold Peak tea machine was observed next to the soda machine. Remove the tea machine from the facility.
The premises shall be free of items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as equipment that is nonfunctional or no longer used.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Employee that was not a certified food manager did not have proof of food handler certification available at the time of inspection. Maintain copies of food handler certifications on-site.
